decision: KEEP ECMAScript build-time declaration projection; FIX selector validation so unsupported siblings and malformed scalar unions fail before output.
constraints: Generate TypeScript declarations and a canonical JSON Schema bundle from the committed API-v1 schema, offline on Node/Linux and Windows.
Reject unsupported schema shapes explicitly; preserve current output bytes and AJV standalone runtime validation. This build tool processes a repository-owned contract, not incoming sensor data.
Do not silently widen a declaration by ignoring sibling assertions. Static types do not replace runtime numeric, string, provenance or timing checks.

alternatives.assessment: KEEP with explicit selector guards: directly emits the required host declaration and canonical JSON artifacts. Twelve counterexamples establish the former gap and its correction; committed-output equality establishes local compatibility. No runtime dependency is added.

Official tool supports OpenAPI 3.0/3.1 to TypeScript and can handle wider schema coverage. That broader acceptance does not itself enforce this component's deliberately closed vocabulary and fixed tuple limits; an independent contract guard would still be required. Reassess for broader SDK generation.

Official multi-language schema/type/converter generator is credible if multiple owned SDKs share a generation boundary. This component requires TypeScript declarations plus a preserved schema bundle and explicit unsupported-shape rejection; replacing it would not remove that guard. No cross-language output requirement is implemented here.

Credible schema-to-Rust code generation with native typed output. Its documented output is Rust types, while this boundary requires TypeScript declarations; a separate TS emitter and Node packaging integration would remain. No native parsing throughput requirement justifies migration of this small offline build step.

limits: Only the supported selector subset is corrected; this is not a complete JSON Schema metaschema validator or general intersection engine.

References and anyOf permit title/description annotations only. const/enum additionally permit matching scalar type; sibling assertions require an explicit future design. Enum values must be nonempty, unique, finite JSON scalars.
No alternative compiler benchmark or universal language ranking; selection follows output format and rejection semantics. No browser, hardware, hard-real-time or certification evidence is created.
